[[File:Ryan Giggs with PL trophy in 2008.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Ryan Giggs holding the Premier League trophy|[[Ryan Giggs]] has more [[Premier League]] medals than any other player, winning the title 13 times with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].]]

The [[Premier League]] is an [[association football]] league that serves as the top tier of the [[English football league system]]. The league was founded in 1992 when the clubs of the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] decided to break away from [[the Football League]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/history |title=History |publisher=Premier League |access-date=23 April 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708150255/https://www.premierleague.com/history |archive-date=8 July 2017}}</ref> as a commercially independent entity that negotiated its own broadcast and sponsorship agreements.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://inews.co.uk/sport/football/football-indepth/premier-league-first-weekend-1992/ |title=The Premier League's first weekend in 1992 shows how much has changed |first=Alex |last=Nelson |newspaper=i |location=London |date=10 August 2017 |access-date=23 April 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422202015/https://inews.co.uk/sport/football/football-indepth/premier-league-first-weekend-1992/ |archive-date=22 April 2018}}</ref>

Since the [[2012–13 Premier League|2012–13 season]], a player needs to have played in a minimum of five matches for a title-winning team to qualify for a medal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/05/who-gets-premier-league-winners-medal |title=The Premier League's rules for giving out winners medals are brutally harsh |first=Luke |last=Kerr-Dineen |website=For The Win |publisher=Gannett Company |date=22 May 2017 |access-date=23 April 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422205515/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/05/who-gets-premier-league-winners-medal |archive-date=22 April 2018}}</ref> This is down from the previous standard of 10 matches played.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/who-gets-premier-league-medals-14538360 |title=Which Manchester City players will get Premier League medals? |first=Stuart |last=Brennan |newspaper=Manchester Evening News |date=17 April 2018 |access-date=23 April 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422212312/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/who-gets-premier-league-medals-14538360 |archive-date=22 April 2018}}</ref> At the discretion of the Premier League board, additional medals can be awarded to players who played less than five matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pulse-static-files.s3.amazonaws.com/premierleague/document/2017/09/27/bfb4b8a2-55c4-45c4-a5f0-c2abbd6a6f4b/PL_Handbook_2017-18_FINAL.pdf |title=Premier League: Handbook: 2017/18 |page=108 |publisher=Premier League |access-date=23 April 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422204200/https://pulse-static-files.s3.amazonaws.com/premierleague/document/2017/09/27/bfb4b8a2-55c4-45c4-a5f0-c2abbd6a6f4b/PL_Handbook_2017-18_FINAL.pdf |archive-date=22 April 2018}}</ref> This special dispensation is usually reserved for back-up goalkeepers and players who did not make the minimum number of appearances through injury.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-news-asmir-begovic-premier-league-winners-medal-doesnt-deserve-one-rethink-a7740586.html |title=Asmir Begovic calls for Premier League winners' medal rethink as Chelsea goalkeeper says he doesn't deserve one |first=Jack |last=De Menezes |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=17 May 2017 |access-date=23 April 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422222040/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-news-asmir-begovic-premier-league-winners-medal-doesnt-deserve-one-rethink-a7740586.html |archive-date=22 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/title-medal-hope-for-red-giants-991862 |title=Title medal hope for Red giants |first=Stuart |last=Brennan |newspaper=Manchester Evening News |date=11 May 2007 |access-date=26 May 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423165946/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/title-medal-hope-for-red-giants-991862 |archive-date=23 April 2018}}</ref> For the first season in [[1992–93 FA Premier League|1992–93]], players received a miniature version of the trophy rather than a medal.<ref>{{cite magazine |first=Ryan |last=Giggs |date=February 2005 |title=e11evenses |magazine=The Official Manchester United Magazine |publisher=Future |issue=150 |page=38 |quote=Our first Premiership win in 1992/93 was the only time we've ever received a miniature trophy instead of a medal.}}</ref>

As of the end of the [[2025–26 Premier League|2025–26 season]], seven clubs have won the title – [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] –<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engchamp.html |title=England – List of Champions |first=James M. |last=Ross |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |date=28 April 2025 |access-date=2 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922085028/http://www.rsssf.com/tablese/engchamp.html |archive-date=22 September 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> with 683 medals awarded to 344 players. Eleven players have won the title with more than one club. Having won 13 Premier League championships, Manchester United have more title-winning players to their name than any other club, with 86 players awarded 247 medals. [[Ryan Giggs]], who spent his entire career at the club,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/may/21/ryan-giggs-career-history-english-football-manchester-united |title=Was Ryan Giggs' playing career the best in the history of English football? |first=Paul |last=Campbell |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=21 May 2014 |access-date=9 June 2018 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180608225603/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/may/21/ryan-giggs-career-history-english-football-manchester-united |archive-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> has won more medals than any other player with 13. Nearly a third of medals have been awarded to English players, with the next most frequent nationalities of winners being French and Brazilian.

==Key==
*The list is initially ordered first by number of medals, then by season, and then if necessary by alphabetical order.
*Position key: GK – [[Goalkeeper (association football)|Goalkeeper]]; DF – [[Defender (association football)|Defender]]; MF – [[Midfielder]]; FW – [[Forward (association football)|Forward]].
*Club (X) denotes the number of times a player won a medal with that club.
